parsed.title: Discussion on taxes, domain purchase, app viability, and potential scam

claims.text: User P1 claims that paying 500 UAH to aunt Sveta helped avoid larger penalties by correctly resubmitting declarations.
User P1 states that the tax inspector was previously approving declarations without review and later reprimanded.
User P3 says the whole tax correction procedure takes about an hour with Excel, at most a day.
User P1 emphasizes that the main difficulty is correctly identifying which column to adjust, not the calculation itself.
User P1 notes that the calculator works only for hryvnia‑based FOPs, requiring conversion of all transactions to the day's exchange rate.
User P2 mentions they haven't even bought a domain yet.
User P4 jokes that they wouldn't invest in a domain for this project.
User P4 describes the domain as a “silly thing that won’t evaporate even in heat” implying low priority.
User P1 lists many disadvantages of a web‑based product compared to Android/iOS, including poor SEO, no external traffic, no ad revenue, and low user retention.
User P1 shares a podcast insight recommending fast delivery (< 1 week) and a cross‑platform stack like Flutter.
User P4 questions whether there is any demand, suggesting at least ten people must be willing to pay 299 UAH.
User P4 states the app is positioned as a local‑first bundle with limited online features and that the paid part is just a bundle.
User P4 calls the project a “free vibe‑code” experiment with questionable value.
User P4 accuses the author of being a scammer.
User P5 confirms the accusation with “по факту”.
User P5 describes the project as a “vibe‑code”.
